continuity_scope: A character-layer pass restricted to Glen Cook's The Black Company, using the Tor Books edition ISBN 9781250781208. It is the first novel only, not the full Books of the North, South, or Glittering Stone sequence. Chapter/annal-section locators are used rather than unverified transferred pagination.
coverage_rule: Include Croaker; named individual Company command figures and exemplars materially involved in the novel's military choices; named individual Taken or rulers who directly act in the war; and the named individual adversary central to the final conflict. This eight-person cohort is not every named mercenary or title-name.
omissions: All later Black Company novels, Books of the South/Glittering Stone, Port of Shadows, and adaptation/game continuities.
The Black Company, Rebel forces, Taken as a category, armies, military offices, magic, the Lady's empire, places, prophecies, and artifacts as nodes.
Named but non-cohort soldiers, officers, Taken, rebels, and local figures.
uncertainties: Croaker is the Company's annalist and a participant; his military account is partial, compressed, and not omniscient about motives or off-page events.
Aliases and title-names can conceal or shift identity; records preserve the novel's naming state rather than later resolution.
War, execution, coercion, injury, and mass violence are present; descriptions are concise and non-graphic.
evidence_basis: Narrative claims are tied to the declared printed novel by annal/chapter sequence. Tor's official record establishes the edition and first-novel/mercenary/Lady context. No fan wiki or Wikipedia is canonical evidence.

citations.locator: Tor product record; first book in Chronicles of The Black Company; official description
supports: Declared edition and official mercenary/Lady/White Rose series context.
